chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Illness, her daughter's birth and the Village Vanguard anniversary
summary: She was ill after returning, her daughter was born in 1945, and she thought about stopping as styles changed.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: didn't know where I was because - and I wasn't making any recordings. So nobody knew where I was or what I was doing. But I was working quite regularly. I didn't do any radio or anything. I didn't get in on the ground floor with television. I did a couple of interviews and things like that throught friends of mine but so far as getting any spots or regular shows, I just wasn't in the running. I didn't have the management. I was freelancing, so to speak, which I still am. And then after Village Vanguard I got the opportunity to go out to Honolulu and this was in the '50s now. And I did Honolulu, and when I came back that's when I retired.

First of all when I came back I wasn't well. I had to go into the hospital. I had an operation. And when I came out I decided that this was an ideal time to just quit. I was going to be laid up for awhile anyway recuperating and at the same time Paula was coming out of elementary school to Junior High School.
1945. And I had celebrated twenty year anniversary at the Village Vanguard, you know, so I figured twenty years, that's a pretty good run.

So I figured I'd stop and things were changing and styles were changing. You know, you can nearly wear yourself out, you know, you keep going down, down, down. So I'm like, Pearl Bailey would say, I quit while I was ahead. And I didn't look back. I just got out of it completely. Naturally I listened. I was with Cliff, you know, I'd go to clubs and things like that. And of course I had records to listen to. I had to listen to Paula's records. I had to listen to rock and all this, so I really never left home.
